messages:
Sofia: Heads up — during the v2.3.0 release tests a CI job printed what looks like an API key in the debug output. Can someone triage? Link to PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/1423

Mike: Which job exactly? artifact or console output?

Sofia: integration-test-run-187 on ci-ops. Snippet I grabbed from the runner logs:
```
[2026-03-17T14:22:11Z] DEBUG config_loader: read env: API_KEY=sk-stage-4b3a6f2cxxxxxx (truncated)
```
Looks truncated but the `sk-` prefix and first 8 chars are present.

Jane: If it starts with `sk-` assume it may be a live key. Who set that env?

Sofia: It was added in the PR above — we accidentally set the integration secret as a plaintext env in .github/workflows/deploy.yml for the CI job. Not a secret ref. 

deploy-bot: Notifying owners: @jane @mike @eng-ops :rotating_light: 

Mike: Ok immediate plan: 1) check whether the value came from Vault/SSM or was pasted into the workflow; 2) check if the CI artifact containing the log got uploaded to S3 or other storage; 3) rotate/disable the key if it's live; 4) scrub logs/artifacts. @jane can you take vault/permissions and rotation?

Jane: On it. Running `vault kv get secret/ci/integration` and checking `metadata.last_rotated` and access logs. Also running CloudTrail lookup for GetSecretValue and the CI role.

audit-bot: CloudTrail entry found: GetSecretValue from role arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-runner at 2026-03-17T14:22:10Z — matches the job window.

Sofia: I also found the debug artifact at ci-artifacts/integ/187/debug.log. It wasn't publicly exposed but may persist in the bucket.

Mike: If the secret is backed by Vault but was echoed into logs, still treat it as exposed. Rotate the secret. If it's KMS-encrypted in a parameter store, rotate the parameter and re-encrypt. Also add a short-term policy: remove plaintext env from repo and re-run tests after secret rotation.

Jane: Created ticket SEC-1129 with remediation: rotated secret, revoked old credential, removed plaintext from workflow, set workflow to use GitHub Actions secrets (KMS-backed). Added CI job to re-run tests with rotated secret. Tagging @sofia for verification.

Sofia: Verified the new runs (integration-test-run-188) do not print keys. I scrubbed the old artifact and requested object hard-delete from S3. Also added a redaction step to the CI pipeline that masks patterns matching `sk-[A-Za-z0-9]{8,}` and long base64-like tokens.

Mike: Good. Follow-ups: add a pre-commit / CI lint to fail PRs containing obvious secret patterns, add a line to the PR checklist, and run a quick sweep over recent release branches for similar mistakes. Thanks for the fast response :+1:

Jane: Will add the checklist item and push a small repo-level secret-scan workflow.

Sofia: One more ask — can we get an HSM/KMS policy doc updated that covers CI best-practices (no plaintext envs, use vault-agent or secrets manager)? I'll draft and share.

Mike: Please do. Also note for the postmortem: how the workflow got a plaintext secret (human copy/paste), and how our CI allowed it. We'll include mitigation and timeline in SEC-1129.

Sofia: Draft incoming. Thanks everyone for the quick help.
